question_text: A 4×4 integer grid must contain every integer 1..16 exactly once. Assume every value is in that range. Construct complete_grid(grid) in Python using a 16-element flag list, returning True if and only if the grid is complete. Mark the flag at value-1 while traversing, then check all flags. Do not use sets or sorting.
adaptation_rationale: Preserves flag-index mapping and nested traversal; Python 4×4 context, explicit size/range assumptions and reasoned uniqueness.

marking_points.criterion: Traverses all elements in each row.
Sets that flag to mark presence.
Inspects every flag or stops when missing flag found.
Returns False if any flag is unmarked.
Returns True only if all 16 flags are marked; fixed 16 input cells imply unique values.

acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent technically correct wording or valid implementation earning the specified independent points.
partial_credit_notes: Award each stated point independently up to the total; do not double-credit the same idea.

verification.technical: Concrete marking points independently reasoned from the defined context and exact 2027 scope.
verification.code_check: Executable checks saved under checks/ where applicable.

test_code:
good=[list(range(r*4+1,r*4+5)) for r in range(4)]
assert complete_grid(good)
bad=[row[:] for row in good];bad[3][3]=1;assert not complete_grid(bad)
